surfaces.part: packed-earth ground texture with path network, ruts and footprints

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 256x192 ground texture. Every row is 256 px wide, so there is no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical face. The column scans show only mottled dirt tones alternating between L≈60-118 with no horizontal banding or edge line. This is flat terrain seen from above, with lighter path patches, ruts and footprints on darker dirt. It matches the terrain kind and has no standing front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows about 5 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, so it is above grass and slightly below paving. Near-flat coverage is 2%, so there are no large flat fills; the surface is broken up by mottled clumps and speckle dots. There is no outline, which fits the feathered-edge brief, and the dark edge pixels carry a brown tint (0% neutral). The earth ramp is only about 4 steps (light packed earth, mid, dark clump, speckle) against 5-6 in Beodeul. The texture is a repetitive mottled pattern that tiles visibly, with a regular blotch motif in each tile. The lighter path reads weakly: faint rectangular lighter zones, with no clear ruts, footprints, crossings or dead ends. The path network is hard to read and low in contrast. The piece is competent and close to the reference level, but it is a little shallower and more uniform than the references, so I am failing it on doubt.

surfaces.part: packed earth path ground texture (tiled dirt with lighter path areas)

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 256-wide by 192-row terrain texture of packed dirt, with no silhouette, no outline and no standing volume. The width is 256 on every row, so there is no ellipse profile. The column scans show only mottled dirt tones (L=60-118) alternating with no front-edge line or eave shadow. It is a flat ground tile seen from above, with lighter path patches, ruts and footprints, and it has no front face. For terrain this is the expected flat ground reading.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 5 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 2%, so there are no large flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, and the path has no outline, as the brief asks. It reads as 4 or so distinct earth ramp steps (light path, mid dirt, dark clumps, and sparse grey flecks) with dotted grain and clump texture throughout. Weaknesses: the lighter path reads as faint, blocky, rectangular patches that follow tile boundaries rather than a clear network with crossings and dead ends, and the wheel ruts and footprints are barely legible. The soil clump pattern also repeats identically from tile to tile, so it looks stamped. The lightness ramp is narrow, with only 7 raw colours in total, which is shallower than the 5-6 steps Beodeul uses per material. This is a borderline case, and it fails on the thin shading ramp, the repeated stamped texture, and the path shapes that are not clearly readable.

There is no outline, which matches the brief, and the path edges feather into the dirt. It has speckle and clump texture in several browns plus small pebbles, so it has no real flat fills. The weaknesses are structural. The path is only a slightly lighter band, and the light/mid/dark ramp is shallow at about 4 steps against the 5-6 of Beodeul. The wheel ruts and footprints are barely visible, and the path network with crossings and dead ends is hard to read. Per-tile density is on par with the references by the numbers, but by eye the shading is less varied and less crafted than the reference paving, so it falls just short of the bar.
